title: Mobile savings groups for smallholder farmers
summary: A project works with farmers' savings groups in a rural district. It helps them save through mobile money, with a wallet that stays locked until planting season, so farmers have cash for seed and fertiliser when they need it.
whyThisWorks: The problem names a timing gap: farmers have cash at harvest but not at planting. Each activity answers part of that gap. Outputs are counts the project team controls. Outcomes separate saving behaviour (short-term) from coping and investment (medium-term). The assumptions draw on evaluation lessons: savings groups tend to protect households in bad times more than they raise average income, and pressure to share money with friends and family can undo saving.

items: Most smallholder farmers have cash at harvest but not at planting. Savings kept at home get spent or shared, and banks are far away.
assumptions: Farmers want to buy more inputs if they have cash at planting

indicators.text: Share of member households using fertiliser
indicators.target: Tracked for context. Targets are set at outcome level.

items: Help 60 savings groups move their savings onto mobile money
Offer a planting-savings wallet that stays locked until planting season
Train group treasurers to keep digital records
Hold input fairs with local agro-dealers before planting
assumptions: Mobile network and cash-out agents reach every village
A mobile money provider agrees to offer a locked wallet

indicators.text: Number of savings groups saving through mobile money
indicators.target: 60 groups by the end of year 1

items: 60 groups, about 1,500 members, saving through mobile money
60 treasurers trained and keeping digital records
Two input fairs a year in each of 6 market towns
assumptions: Fees stay low enough for small deposits
Members trust the mobile money provider

indicators.text: Members with an active planting-savings wallet
indicators.meansOfVerification: Provider account data, shared with members' consent

items: Members save more and keep savings until planting
More members buy fertiliser and improved seed on time
Group records are accurate and easy to check
assumptions: Family and friends don't pressure members to share savings

indicators.text: Average member savings balance at the start of planting season

items: Households cope better with bad harvests and lean seasons
Farm investment rises among members who want to invest
assumptions: Input and crop prices stay within a normal range
Rains are not poor several years in a row

indicators.text: Share of member households skipping meals in the lean season
indicators.meansOfVerification: Household survey before and after the lean season

items: Smallholder households have enough food and income all year
assumptions: No market or climate shock bigger than savings can absorb

indicators.text: Share of households short of food during the lean season

draftPairs.improved: Households cope better with bad harvests and lean seasons
draftPairs.why: Evaluations of savings groups found they mostly help families absorb shocks, not raise average income. An outcome should match what the evidence suggests is realistic.

draftPairs.improved: Help 60 savings groups move their savings onto mobile money
draftPairs.why: The first version is a goal, not something the team does. The improved version says what happens, with whom and how many.
